name: MonarchFavicon
title: Favicon
summary: A site's icon at a fixed size, with a tile showing the first letter of the site name while there is no image.
whenToUse: Beside a link, a domain or a connected service, so people recognise the site at a glance.
whenNotToUse: For a person or an organization use an avatar. For an icon that stands for an action use MonarchIcon.
api: @Composable fun MonarchFavicon(image: Painter?, name: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, label: String? = null, size: MonarchFaviconSize = MonarchFaviconSize.Sm, shape: MonarchFaviconShape = MonarchFaviconShape.Rounded)
enum class MonarchFaviconSize { Sm, Md, Lg }
enum class MonarchFaviconShape { Rounded, Circle, Square }

options.name: image
options.description: The icon loaded by the app, or null to show the letter tile.

options.name: name
options.description: The site's name or domain; its first letter or digit is shown on the tile.

options.name: label
options.description: What TalkBack reads. Without it the favicon is decoration and hidden.

states.name: image
states.description: The picture is fitted inside the tile and clipped to the shape.

states.name: fallback
states.description: A tile in the muted background color with a subtle border and one upper-case letter in the muted text color. Shown while loading, after a failure and when there is no icon.

appearance: The letter tile uses the muted background, the subtle border and the muted text color in every theme. The image is shown as it is.
platformNotes: The web Favicon takes a domain or URL, an optional resolveSrc function and a size in pixels, and checks that the URL is safe to load. Android follows the Monarch picture convention instead: the app loads the icon with its own pipeline and passes a Painter, so there is no URL to check and Monarch never calls a favicon service. iOS also offers a URL initialiser; Android does not, because Monarch ships no image loader. Sizes are the named Sm, Md and Lg, as on iOS. The tile keeps its size at every font size, as Android icons do; on iOS it scales with Dynamic Type.
accessibility: Without a label the favicon is hidden from TalkBack, because the site name is normally written next to it.
With a label it is one TalkBack element with the image role, read as the label.
Not interactive, so it has no touch target.
edgeCases: A name without a letter or digit shows "?".
The letter is upper-cased in the default locale, so "istanbul" gives a dotted capital I in Turkish.
A letter outside the Basic Multilingual Plane is kept whole.
The image is fitted, not cropped: an icon with another aspect ratio leaves space at the sides.

examples.code:
MonarchFavicon(
    image = samplePainter(),
    name = "search.example",
    label = "Example Search",
    size = MonarchFaviconSize.Lg,
    shape = MonarchFaviconShape.Circle,
)
